sentences.text: In order to decide whether plaintiff has been defamed or not, the court has to see whether the essentials of defamation have been satisfied or not.
18. Defamation is an injury to the reputation of a person, which is harm made to the character or goodwill of a person.
In India, there is no distinction made between statement made orally or in permanent form and both are offences under the law of tort as civil wrong as well as crime under IPC.

The essentials of defamation are as follows:
1. Statement must be defamatory which means that it must result in lowering the moral character of a person in the eyes of the society or any other person.

In the landmark case of P. Chowdhary v. Manjulata, AIR 1997 Raj 170, wherein it was held that "Statement published in a newspaper which is untrue and without any justification affected the reputation of her family as well as her marriage prospects so the defendants were held liable for her defamation".
2. The statement must refer to the plaintiff.

sentences.text: If the statement is made without an intent to defame but results in defamation of the plaintiff, the defendant will still be held liable.

sentences.text: 19. Defendant can plead his defence by way of the following defences.

20. Since defendant has been proceeded ex-parte in this matter, hence oral as well as documentary evidence led by plaintiff remains uncontroverted and unchallenged, defendants have not brought any defence pleading truth, fair comment or privilege.
Hence, the Court finds no ground to disbelieve the testimony of plaintiff's witnesses.

Plaintiff has been able to prove all the ingredients which is that the statement published was defamatory; that it was referred to the plaintiff as it was mentioned by name on a WhatsApp group containing 250 people who all got to read it apart from the plaintiff.
Plaintiff also examined other two witnesses apart from herself to show that her reputation was tarnished by the acts of the defendants in the eyes of several persons.
21. Documentary evidence led by plaintiff's witness deserves to be accepted on its face value.

24.In view of above discussion, the suit is decree ex-parte.
Following reliefs are being granted to plaintiff:
(a) The plaintiff is granted permanent injunction against defendants nos.1 and 2 and their accomplices from publishing/sending/circulating/posting/propagating any f u r t h e r u n v e r i f i e d , u n s u b s t a n t i a t e d a n d d e f a m a t o r y s t a t e m e n t s /
publishing/sending/circulating/posting/propagating any kind of abusive or threatening or intimidating or defamatory content in any manner whatsoever, either by print or electronically.
Plaintiff is also granted mandatory injunction directing the defendants to delete the group 'Urgent' remove her personal photographs, videos and audios from social media and make a public apology in a newspaper with national circulation.
Plaintiff is entitled to recovery of Rs.10 Lacs against both the defendants alongwith interest @10%
per annum from the date of tendering the money till the date of its return.
(c) As far damages are concerned, defendants are directed to pay Rs.1 Lac each to the plaintiff as damages.
25. Ex-parte decree sheet be prepared accordingly.
The present ex- parte decree is passed subject to filing of deficient court fees, if any.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
